questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The history of home computers
How to repair old technology
Why new gadgets are so expensive
Old technology that is still used today, and why
questions.why: They hear about old tech which continues to be used today.

questions.q: Which example of old technology still being used is NOT mentioned?
options: Floppy disks used by the Japanese government
Fax machines used by banks
Music cassettes making a comeback
Magnetic tape used at CERN
questions.why: Phil mentions Japan's floppy disks, cassettes and CERN's tape reels, but not banks using fax machines.

questions.q: What reasons does Georgie give for some old technology refusing to die?
options: It is cheaper and lighter
Governments make people use it
People still love it, or it still works fine
New technology is too hard to find and too expensive to buy
questions.why: She says maybe people still love it, or because 'if it ain't broke, don't fix it'.

questions.q: What is HAR-V, designed by NASA engineer Jonathan Sauder?
options: A clockwork rover powered by the wind on Venus
A solar-powered robot designed to explore the surface of Mars
A computer for the space station
A new type of rocket engine
questions.why: He describes it as a mechanical clockwork rover powered by Venus's winds.

questions.q: Why did Jonathan use clockwork for the rover?
options: Because ordinary electronics won't work in Venus's conditions
Because it was cheaper
Because clockwork is faster and stronger than any electric motor
Because NASA had no batteries
questions.why: Georgie says conditions on Venus mean ordinary electronics simply won't work.

questions.q: Why does Phil mention electrical plugs?
options: To show how dangerous old plugs are
To explain how the rover gets power
To give an example of tech that would be too much work to change
To say that all countries around the world now use the same kind of plug
questions.why: He says standardising plugs would be better, 'but imagine the work involved!'

questions.q: What does presenter Chris Vallance say about the QWERTY keyboard?
options: It is the fastest layout ever made
It may not be the best layout for typing quickly
It was invented especially for court reporters who type very fast
It is no longer used
questions.why: He says it is 'perhaps not the most efficient layout in terms of the speed of typing'.

questions.q: Why will Dr Tacye Phillipson keep using a QWERTY keyboard?
options: She types faster than court reporters
Her museum doesn't allow staff to use any other kind of keyboard
Special keyboards are too expensive
She's used to it and doesn't want to learn a complicated one
questions.why: She says it's the layout we're all used to, and she doesn't want to learn a complicated one.
